purpose: Resolve final Phase3 accepted learner concept black cottonwood under project POWO/WCVP accepted backbone. Explicitly retain FNA/USDA alternate name Populus trichocarpa as synonym; taxonomic disagreement noted; prevent claimed/installed duplicate. Install exact Populus trichocarpa field photo under Kew synonym crosswalk using Wikimedia Commons independently reviewed CC BY-SA 4.0 image; physically verify and strip EXIF/GPS. Public web display allowed with photographer attribution, source/license links, CC BY-SA adaptation duties. No native-to-Texas assertion, no county audit or Cloudflare deployment.

selected.taxonomic_note: POWO/WCVP accepts Populus tristis Fisch. and treats Populus trichocarpa Torr. & A.Gray ex Hook. as a synonym; Flora of North America and USDA use Populus trichocarpa as the working accepted name. These refer to the same Western North American black cottonwood concept here; preserve BOTH scientific names and the alternative-taxonomy caution rather than silently dismissing the FNA treatment. Do not create a duplicate Populus trichocarpa card.
selected.native_range_note: POWO native range lists Alaska, Western Canada, western states, Baja California Norte; Texas not listed. Central Texas native-range or introduced/invasive badge has NOT been certified. County nativity research remains deferred.
selected.look_here_first: Find a tall riparian cottonwood with alternate, broadly ovate to heart-shaped finely serrated leaves (spring leaves may look narrower), sticky reddish-brown aromatic winter buds, and pale whitish leaf undersides. Confirm long hanging catkins, cottony seed capsules and twig/bud characters; separate from local Populus deltoides using blade shape, undersides, petiole and fine margin teeth.
